What the numbers say

For the session of Friday, October 30, 2026, the DappGo regime model reads the tracked universe (26 US-listed stocks and ETFs on DappGo's reviewed watchlist) as mixed. SPY is below its 50-day average and above its 200-day average; its 20-day trend is down and realised volatility is in the calm band.

10 of 26 tickers (38%) are priced above their own 20-day moving average, and 16 of 25 (64%) above their 200-day average. That sits between the model's 30% and 55% breadth thresholds, so breadth alone decides nothing here. On the day 3 rose and 23 fell; the median move was −1.78%.

Among sectors with at least two tracked names, Consumer Discretionary had the strongest average move at −1.23% and Technology the weakest at −9.48%, a spread of 8.25 percentage points. The standard deviation of sector averages was 3.48 points; a larger figure means sectors moved less in step.

4 tickers have a 14-day RSI at or below 30 (GOOG, INTC, BABA, NFLX), and none is at or above 70. An RSI extreme records how one-sided recent trading has been. It is not, by itself, evidence that the move is about to reverse.

Against the previous session in this archive (2026-10-29), the share of tickers above the 20-day average held at 38%, and the regime reading stayed mixed.
